{{Short description|Embedding of a Grassmannian into projective space}}
In [[mathematics]],  the '''Plücker map''' embeds the [[Grassmannian]] <math>\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)</math>, whose elements are ''k''-[[Dimension (vector space)|dimensional]] [[Linear subspace|subspace]]s of an ''n''-dimensional [[vector space]] ''V'', either real or complex, in a [[projective space]], thereby realizing it as a [[projective algebraic variety]]. More precisely, the Plücker map [[Embedding|embeds]] <math>\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)</math> into the projectivization <math>\mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V)</math> of the <math>k</math>-th [[exterior power]] of <math>V</math>. The image is algebraic, consisting of the intersection of a number of quadrics defined by the {{slink||Plücker relations}} (see below).

The Plücker embedding was first defined by  [[Julius Plücker]] in the case  [[Plücker coordinates|<math>k=2, n=4</math>]] as a way of describing the lines in [[three-dimensional space]] (which, as [[projective line]]s in [[real projective space]], correspond to two-dimensional subspaces of a four-dimensional vector space). The image of that embedding is the [[Klein quadric]] in '''RP'''<sup>5</sup>.

[[Hermann Grassmann]] generalized Plücker's embedding to arbitrary ''k'' and ''n''. The homogeneous coordinates of the image of the Grassmannian <math> \mathrm{Gr}(k,V)</math> under the Plücker embedding, relative to the basis in the exterior space <math>{\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V </math> corresponding to the natural basis in <math>V = K^n</math> (where <math>K</math> is the base [[Field (mathematics)|field]]) are called [[Plücker coordinates]].

== Definition ==
Denoting by <math>V= K^n</math>  the <math>n</math>-dimensional vector space over the field <math>K</math>, and by
<math> \mathrm{Gr}(k, V)</math> the Grassmannian of <math>k</math>-dimensional subspaces of <math>V</math>, the Plücker embedding is the map ''ι'' defined by

::<math>\begin{array}{cccc}
\iota : \  & \mathrm{Gr}(k, V) & \longrightarrow & \mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V),\\
 &  {W}:=\operatorname{Span}( w_1, \ldots, w_k ) & \longmapsto & [ w_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge w_k ], 
 \end{array}</math>

where <math>(w_1, \dots , w_k)</math> is a basis for the element  <math> {W}\in \mathrm{Gr}(k, V)</math> and <math> [ w_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge w_k ]</math> is the projective [[equivalence class]] of the element <math> w_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge w_k \in {\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V </math> of the <math>k</math>th exterior power of <math>V</math>.

This is an embedding of the Grassmannian into the projectivization <math>\mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V)</math>. The image can be completely characterized as the intersection of a number of quadrics, the Plücker quadrics (see below), which are expressed by homogeneous quadratic relations on the  Plücker coordinates (see below) that derive from [[linear algebra]].

The [[bracket ring]] appears as the ring of polynomial functions on <math>{\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V </math>.<ref>{{citation | last1=Björner | first1=Anders |author1-link=Anders Björner| last2=Las Vergnas |author2-link=Michel Las Vergnas| first2=Michel | last3=Sturmfels | first3=Bernd | author3-link=Bernd Sturmfels | last4=White | first4=Neil | last5=Ziegler | first5=Günter |author5-link=Günter M. Ziegler| title=Oriented matroids | edition=2nd | series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Its Applications | volume=46 | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | year=1999 | isbn=0-521-77750-X | zbl=0944.52006 | page=79|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511586507}}</ref>

== Plücker relations ==
The image under the Plücker embedding satisfies a simple set of homogeneous quadratic relations, usually called the '''Plücker relations''', or '''Grassmann–Plücker relations''', defining the intersection of a number of quadrics in <math> \mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V) </math>.  This shows that the Grassmannian embeds as an algebraic subvariety of <math>\mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V)</math> and gives another method of constructing the Grassmannian. To state the Grassmann–Plücker relations, let <math>{W}\in \mathrm{Gr}(k, V) </math> be the <math>k</math>-dimensional subspace spanned by the basis represented by column vectors <math>w_1, \dots, w_k</math>. 
Let <math> [W] </math> be the  <math> n \times k</math> matrix whose columns are  <math>w_1, \dots, w_k</math>; the matrix of <math>W</math> with respect to a different basis is then <math>[W]A</math> for any invertible <math> k \times k</math> matrix <math>A</math>. For any ordered sequence <math>1\le i_1 < \cdots < i_k \le n </math> 
of <math> k </math> integers, let <math> \Delta_{i_1, \dots , i_k} </math> be the determinant of the <math>k \times k</math> submatrix of <math> [W] </math> on the rows <math>(i_1, \dots i_k)</math>; this determinant is called a ''[[minor (linear algebra)|minor]]''. Then <math>\{ \Delta_{i_1, \dots , i_k}\} </math> are the '''[[Plücker coordinates]]''' of the element <math>{W}\in \mathrm{Gr}(k, V) </math>, the linear coordinates of the image <math>\iota({W})\in \mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V)</math> relative to the [[standard basis]] <math>\{e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_k}\}</math> of <math> {\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V </math>. Changing the basis of <math> W </math> just changes the Plücker coordinates by a nonzero factor <math>\det(A)</math>, the determinant of the change of basis matrix,
giving the same point in <math> \mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V) </math>.  

For any two ordered sequences: 
::<math> i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_{k-1}, \quad j_1 < j_2 < \cdots < j_{k+1}</math>
of positive integers <math> 1 \le i_l, j_m \le n </math>, the following homogeneous equations are valid, and determine the image of  <math>W</math> under the Plücker map:<ref>
{{Citation | last1=Griffiths | first1=Phillip | author1-link=Phillip Griffiths | last2=Harris | first2=Joseph | author2-link=Joe Harris (mathematician) | title=Principles of algebraic geometry | page=211| publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]] | location=New York | series=Wiley Classics Library | edition=2nd | isbn=0-471-05059-8 | mr=1288523 | year=1994 | zbl=0836.14001 }} </ref><blockquote><math>\sum_{l=1}^{k+1} (-1)^l \Delta_{i_1, \dots , i_{k-1}, j_l} \Delta_{j_1, \dots , \hat{j}_l, \dots j_{k+1}}=0,
</math></blockquote>where <math> j_1, \dots , \hat{j}_l, \dots j_{k+1} </math> denotes that the term <math> j_l </math> is omitted. These are the '''Plücker relations'''.


When {{math|dim(''V'') {{=}} 4}} and {{math|''k'' {{=}} 2}}, we get <math>\mathrm{Gr}(2, V)</math>, the simplest Grassmannian which is not a projective space, and the above reduces to a single equation. Denoting the coordinates of <math> {\textstyle\bigwedge}^2 V</math> by 
:: <math> \Delta_{ij} = -\Delta_{ji}, \quad 1\le i,j \le 4,</math>
the image of <math>\mathrm{Gr}(2, V)</math> under the Plücker map is defined by the single equation

::<math>\Delta_{12}\Delta_{34} - \Delta_{13}\Delta_{24} + \Delta_{14}\Delta_{23}=0.</math>

In general, many more equations are needed to define the image of the Plücker embedding, as in  ({{EquationNote|1}}), 
but these are not, in general, [[Algebraic independence|algebraically independent]]. The maximal number of algebraically independent relations (on Zariski open sets)
is given by the difference of dimension between <math>\mathbb{P}({\textstyle\bigwedge}^k V)</math> and <math>\mathrm{Gr}(k, V)</math>, which is <math> \tbinom{n}{k} - k(n-k) -1. </math>
